clue.text: Showing directors holding drinking vessel a place for drying out

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an airing is a showing or public broadcast of something
a company's directors make up its board
a cup is a vessel for drinking from

explanation.surface: A display of directors clutching their glasses reads like a boardroom where everyone needs to dry out from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drying out' suggests sobering up, but an AIRING CUPBOARD is the heated cupboard in British homes, usually around the hot water tank, where laundry is dried and aired.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm cupboard round a household boiler or tank is where damp clothes and linen are left to finish drying.

clue.text: Parting with son's awkward, without right maternal bonds?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumble goes around the next piece
awkward letters sit clumsily, so they must be put into a better order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the possessive's S kept
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mother's boy finds leaving home awkward, the parting hard without someone to set him right.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'without' as lacking, but here it means outside: the scrambled letters wrap around R. The question mark marks the definition as figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tied to your mother's apron strings is the idiom for a grown child still dependent on their mother, so they are bonds to her.

clue.text: Traveller in greater need of water has head dropping

indicators.note: the leading letter falls further down the word, so its letters are rearranged in that one way

parts.note: something drier needs water more

explanation.surface: A desert traveller, parched and craving water, has their head drooping.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the head is the top letter: the D of DRIER drops two places down the column to give RIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone travelling on horseback, bicycle or as a passenger on a vehicle.

clue.text: Mobile phone's cases yet to change for starters

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so one piece surrounds the other
mobile means able to move, so these letters are free to shift around

parts.note: taken as written, with the possessive's S

indicators.note: letters that are still to change will be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mobile phone cases are not yet changing for beginners, like a shop note about stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one item, but Mobile is the instruction for the letters of the next word. Both scrambles are separate; the first wraps around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophytes are novices or beginners, people just starting out in something, so starters in that sense.

clue.text: Thus Tom gets in tizzy, after answer given in court

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind what follows it
something given in to a place is put inside it

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
A is the abbreviation for answer
to be in a flap is to be in a tizzy, a state of agitation

explanation.surface: A tomcat on trial gets in a tizzy after giving his answer in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a person: the definition reads 'thus (by this means) a tom gets in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat flap is the small hinged door fitted in a house door so a cat can come in and out.

clue.text: Idealist running military group

parts.note: the Greek philosopher Plato is the founder of philosophical idealism
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: An idealistic commander is running a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a unit of soldiers, a subdivision of a company commanded by a lieutenant.

clue.text: Choose to pen article on start of Rachel Riley's work, say

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to opt is to choose

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above, so one piece comes before the next

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Someone opts to write about Rachel Riley, the numbers presenter on the TV quiz Countdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Riley of Countdown is the decoy; the definition needs only Riley, meaning the painter Bridget Riley. 'Say' shows her work is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget Riley is the best-known British painter of op art, abstract work using geometric patterns to create optical illusions.

clue.text: Flogging Parisian and complaining about it

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly
et is French for and; 'it' points back to this phrase as what goes inside

explanation.surface: A Parisian is beaten and grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Flogging looks like beating, but it is British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is informal British for to sell, and retailing is selling goods to the public.

clue.text: A famous Christian's cycling broadcast

indicators.note: cycling sends letters round in a loop, so the last moves to the front

parts.note: taken as written
Christian Dior, the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A well-known Christian's cycle ride is being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is a first name here, not a faith: the designer Christian Dior. ADIOR's final letter cycles round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is sound transmitted over the airwaves, the medium of broadcasting.

clue.text: European bores knock pretentious American protestors

indicators.note: to bore is to drill a way in, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: a tap is a light knock
E is the abbreviation for European
arty means showily or pretentiously artistic

explanation.surface: A European with tedious opinions knocks pretentious American protesters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like a noun for dull people but is a verb: the E drills into the knock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party is the US conservative protest movement named after the 1773 Boston Tea Party.

clue.text: Heads of publicity back from fashion party

parts.note: a promo is a promotional piece of publicity

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Heads of publicity return from a fashion party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of' looks like a first-letters instruction, but Heads is the definition: headlands. 'Back from' is the selector.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a promontory, a high point of land jutting into the sea, as in Beachy Head.

clue.text: Horny beast hurried over with young King Henry

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ran means hurried
W is the abbreviation for with
Prince Hal, Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

explanation.surface: A horned animal charges past with the youthful Prince Hal.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny means horned, not aroused: the narwhal's single long tusk is a horn of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose males carry a long spiral tusk, the source of the unicorn legend.

clue.text: Expose fraudster, we hear, one in extreme position

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken form, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a fraudster is a liar; the spelling follows the sound

explanation.surface: Exposing a fraudster, as we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a data point or person lying far from the rest, at an extreme position.

clue.text: Kind of deck with sailor not leaving navy

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A sailor refuses to leave the navy and stays on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck sounds nautical alongside sailor and navy, but it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a pack of cards used in fortune-telling, so a kind of deck.

clue.text: How to get a rope for Tommy?

definitions.text: How to get a rope for Tommy?

parts.note: the surface asks how to obtain a length of cord
the setter means: shake up (rock) the letters of a five-letter musical drama and they spell 'a rope'
Tommy is The Who's 1969 album telling a story in songs

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy looks like a British soldier needing kit, but it is The Who's album about a deaf, dumb and blind pinball player.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is the most famous example of a rock-music drama told through a sequence of songs.

clue.text: Belief Manx cat lives with Ralph Fiennes, currently

indicators.note: the Manx breed of cat has no tail, so the word loses its end

parts.note: a panther is a big cat
is means exists or lives
Fiennes plays M, the head of MI6, in the current Bond films

explanation.surface: A tailless Manx cat lives with the actor Ralph Fiennes, a tabloid-style snippet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man. 'Currently' tells you which role: Fiennes has played M since Skyfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the belief or doctrine that God is identical with the universe and nature.

clue.text: Resistant to cooking hotpot, mostly, and fare that's stewed

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down into a mix, so these letters are jumbled
mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resists cooking a hotpot, the stewed fare they mostly get.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatproof dishes withstand high temperatures, so they resist the heat of cooking.

clue.text: Cast's working with 9 non-stop

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are shaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the possessive's S
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: The cast works with the 9-across clue's answer without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The number looks like a cross-reference to 9-across, but it is just the word nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause or interruption, the same as non-stop.

clue.text: Concerned with peak I must climb defended by a savage

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something defended is surrounded and protected, so it goes inside

parts.note: to savage a play is to pan it with a harsh review

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue goes upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A climber is anxious about the summit and needs protection from a wild man.
explanation.walkthrough: Savage is a verb, as critics savage a show, not a wild person.
explanation.definitionFit: Apogean relates to the apogee, the highest point or the moment of a moon or satellite's farthest orbit.

clue.text: Miserable across the Channel, drinking English port

indicators.note: something drinking takes a thing in, so the piece goes inside

parts.note: triste is French for sad; across the Channel from Britain is France
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A miserable Frenchman is drinking English port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a seaport city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Part of air from soprano, grandly making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback runs back the way it came, so the letters go right to left
from means taken out of, so the letters lie inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Part of an aria from a soprano, sung grandly as she returns to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' tempts as a tune, given the soprano, but it is the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas making up nearly one per cent of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Marx's work inspiring leader of revolution that's uncomfortable

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer piece takes the others inside

parts.note: a machine that goes is working

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
ouch is the cry for something painful

explanation.surface: Karl Marx's writing inspires revolution, an uncomfortable thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Karl Marx; the answer is a different Marx, and the 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the moustached, cigar-wielding comic of the Marx Brothers film team.

clue.text: Firm hands maintaining a pale colour

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the pair hold the next piece between them

parts.note: right and left hands, R and L
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's workers keep things a pale colour, like a decorating crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands looks like workers, but it means the two hands, right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange shade named after the colour of the sea organism's skeleton.

clue.text: Putting on thick coat, there's nothing Picaroon's too old for?

parts.note: the setter talking about himself: I am, contracted
past it means too old for something
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The setter pulling on a heavy overcoat jokes there is nothing he is too old for.
explanation.walkthrough: Picaroon is the setter, so the name stands for the setter speaking: I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of laying on paint thickly so brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: I suggest that we put up American monument

indicators.note: put up in a down clue raises the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: 'let's' is how one proposes something we do together
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone proposes erecting an American monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like erecting the monument, but it turns the proposal upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright carved stone slab, a standing monument or gravestone in the ancient world.

clue.text: The absolute best, like the House of Lords in recess

definitions.text: like the House of Lords in recess
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: with no peers present, the members having left

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the UK's upper chamber, whose members are peers; in recess it is literally without any.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without peers has no equal, so is unmatched; an empty Lords chamber is lacking its peers.

clue.text: Gaulish warrior wanting ten daggers

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: Obelix, Asterix's menhir-carrying friend in the French comic
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Gaulish warrior wants ten daggers for the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Daggers are the printer's marks, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli, plural of obelus, are dagger-shaped printers' marks used for footnotes.

clue.text: Get no hearing in criminal case of awful offender, alas

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted out of order
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In a criminal case, an awful offender's plea goes unheard, alas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal case' reads as a court trial, but criminal is the scramble signal and case selects letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that fall on deaf ears are ignored, getting no hearing from those addressed.
